primary_result: The physical mapping supplement completed all 1,000 independent validation scenes and 3,000 selected validation variants, but controlled q recovery was 969/1,000 scenes with a two-sided Wilson 95 percent interval of [0.956335, 0.978076]. Its lower bound was below the frozen 0.99 gate, so the route ended COMPLETED_GATE_FAIL and does not authorize ConvIR-B indoor baseline behavior measurement.
gate_reasons: Qualified dataset identity, all frozen counts, same-scene candidate multiplicities, 1,000-scene validation completion, 3,000-variant physical mapping, zero recorded failures, and zero definition-validation canonical overlap all passed.
Severity coverage was 1,000/1,000 with Wilson lower 0.996173, and identifiable-region coverage was 969/1,000 with Wilson lower 0.956335, above its separate 0.90 coverage gate.
Paired-transmission negative-control separation was 1,000/1,000 with Wilson lower 0.996173, and joint scene qualification was 969/1,000 with Wilson lower 0.956335, above the frozen 0.85 gate.
Controlled q recovery was 969/1,000 with Wilson lower 0.956335, below the decisive 0.99 threshold; this single frozen failure determines the terminal FAIL.
The typed closeout authorizes NONE, so no model selection, training, inference, official indoor baseline measurement, or additional adjacent mapping supplement is authorized.
competing_explanation: Reported q errors in identifiable cells were numerically negligible (validation maximum 4.29e-14), while the same 31 scenes drove both incomplete identifiable-region coverage and controlled-q scene failure. The failed 0.99 gate may therefore reflect limited local identifiability under the frozen region and denominator definition rather than incorrect q algebra. This post-result distinction cannot relax or reinterpret the preregistered FAIL; it can only motivate a separately governed orthogonal measurement-field or region-definition question.
limitations: This is development-screening evidence for synthetic indoor ITS only, not confirmation, causal evidence, perceptual validation, or deployment evidence.

The physical mapping chooses the unique minimum-RMSE haze under a synthetic constant-RGB-airlight model; some best-to-second ratios were close to one, so uniqueness does not establish broad real-haze construct validity.
Transmission is synthetic optical thickness and cannot be transported to outdoor or real-haze restoration demand.
No model, module, checkpoint, training, inference, SOTS, OTS, Haze4K test, NH-HAZE, outdoor, canary, confirmation, or locked-test data were used.
Outdoor calibration remains a mandatory independent route, and this indoor FAIL neither supplies nor invalidates an outdoor measurement design.
